name: Redis bundled jemalloc built with --with-lg-page=16 (64KiB PAGE) running on a 4KiB-page kernel
required_postconditions: os_page_detect() <= PAGE, with PAGE == 65536 - a kernel page of 4096 satisfies this and jemalloc boots normally
the allocator rounds everything to 64KiB, wasting address space and RSS but remaining correct on a 4KiB kernel
the configuration is only rejected when the kernel page is LARGER than the compiled-in PAGE

failure_sink.description: same sink as the default build - abort() at pages.c:763 - but on this host the guard at pages.c:760 is not taken, because 4096 > 65536 is false. The sink is declared so the severity model sees it; it is not reached.

source_locations.symbol: [AS_HELP_STRING([--with-lg-page=<lg-page>], [Base 2 log of system page size])] - the build knob that makes PAGE differ from the host page

extraction_limitations: this is the crux: required_page_size can only encode 'page size == N'. The program's actual predicate is 'host page size <= N'. Encoding the 64KiB build faithfully in this schema forces a claim the program never makes

no Redis build script in this tree passes --with-lg-page; this models the configuration distributions use to ship one aarch64 binary across 4KiB/16KiB/64KiB kernels, which is the documented purpose of the option

x_campaign.rationale: rule_page_size compares 65536 against the probed 4096 for equality and fires RS-VM-0006 Proven/Unsupported. I expect that to be wrong: jemalloc's own guard is an inequality that this host passes, so a --with-lg-page=16 build runs correctly on a 4KiB kernel.
x_campaign.note_after_fix: Rewritten to at_most once the relation field existed. jemalloc pages.c checks  - it demands the host page be AT MOST the compiled size and runs correctly on a smaller one. The equality-only reading produced a critical false positive.
x_campaign.expectation_revised_because: The original UNSUPPORTED prediction was written when the contract used page-size EQUALITY. jemalloc pages.c checks `if (os_page > PAGE)` - an AT MOST bound - so the contract was corrected against the source and the prediction updated with it. The old value is recorded here rather than quietly overwritten.
